title: Book Two · Chapter 119: The Brown Notebook
story:
Rain keeps them indoors the next Sunday. Dad takes a brown notebook from the high shelf. He needs an old customer's telephone number for Mr Sun.

Ronan clears the table for him. The cover is soft at the edge. Inside are dates, names, and small columns of money.

“Is this from the old shop?”

“Yes. Part of it.”

Dad turns a page and stops beside a short line. He copies a number onto a separate slip.

Ronan sees three amounts below one job.

“Why are there three?”

“First payment. Cost of the wood. Money I returned.”

“Returned?”

“The job was late. Part of it was wrong. I agreed to return some money.”

Ronan looks at the first amount. It seems large.

“But you still had most of it.”

Dad turns the notebook toward him.

“The wood cost this much. The other parts cost this much. Then I worked for four days.”

“Where is the four days?”

Dad points to the blank space beside the sums.

“I did not count it here.”

Ronan reads the figures again. “So you did not earn that first amount.”

“No.”

The rain grows harder on the roof. Mum moves a finished cloth bag away from the window. She looks at the notebook, then returns to her own table.

“Did someone make you promise four days?” Ronan asks.

“No. I said I could do it.”

“Why?”

“I wanted the job. I thought I could finish the other work fast.”

Ronan waits. Dad does not call the customer cruel. He does not say the wood is to blame.

“Did you know it would be late?”

“Not at first. Later I knew I needed more time. I did not tell him soon enough.”

Dad closes one hand on the edge of the notebook.

Ronan wants to say this is the same as the guide. But Dad's job paid for food and rent. Ronan looks again at the money Dad returned.

“Do you count the time now?”

“At Mr Sun's, yes. We record the jobs and the hours.”

“Every minute?”

“Not every cup of tea. Enough to know the real work.”

Mum says, “His cups of tea need their own book.”

Dad looks at his empty cup. “A short book today.”

Ronan takes it to the kitchen and fills it. When he returns, Dad is checking the customer's telephone number. He shuts the notebook and leaves it on the table.

The rain eases. Ronan puts the cup on a clear corner, well away from the old pages. Dad thanks him and checks the copied number once more before he folds the slip.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

column＝栏；payment＝付款；hours＝工时；rent＝房租。

## 理解问题

1. 为什么首笔收入不等于真正赚到的钱？
2. Dad承认自己什么时候没有及时告知客户？

## 读句子

**Dad / turns the notebook / toward him.** Dad／把笔记本／转向他。
